title: Student government plans a push on campus activities
body: The Herald of 21 September 1967 carried Gary Hunt's report that student government was planning ahead to boost campus activities. The archive holds the issue as a contents listing, so the headline is all the record gives.
why: Cut the claim that this fell in William Menser's year as first student regent: the separately elected seat was still an open campaign question that autumn, and the record supports only the article itself, which I confirmed in the issue listing.

title: The Association billed to open the Associated Students year
body: Associated Students billed a concert by the Association to open its entertainment year, announced in the Herald of 10 October 1968. The issue of 24 October carried photographs of the concert and an interview with the group, so it was played, but neither issue listing gives the night it happened.
why: Demoted the date to month-only because 10 October was just the issue date of the advance billing, and added the 24 October issue, which I checked and which carries the concert photographs and an interview with the band.

title: Lyne's account: entertainment becomes a cultural programme
body: In a signed statement in the 1971 Talisman, president John Lyne wrote that the entertainment side of Associated Students had been expanded into a cultural programmes concept, that big-name concerts continued but names outside the top forty such as Ravi Shankar had been brought in, and that theatrical events had been sponsored, including the co-sponsorship of "1776". He recorded a student-run lecture series as that year's significant addition, said the student discount programme with local merchants had been maintained, and said the organisation was working towards a legal service for students that would include a legal defence fund and a student advocates' corps.

src.label: 1971 Talisman, pp. 66-67, signed statement by John Lyne

why: The rejection was a fact-checker error: I searched the volume's own full text and every clause is in Lyne's signed statement, which runs pp. 66-67 and ends "John Lyne, president, Associated Students"; I only demoted the date to year-only, since a yearbook carries no day.

title: The year's programme summed up in the yearbook
body: The 1972 Talisman summarised Linda Jones's year under the heading "A.S. makes great strides in implementing new programs": in entertainment, mini-concerts, a coffee house in West Hall and the Gaslight film series joined several top-name musical groups and lecturers. The same volume records that Associated Students conducted the elections for class officers, Who's Who and Homecoming queen, held the October mock election for governor, ran a symposium at which students could question administrators, sponsored the Homecoming dance, and revived the Kentucky Student Association among the state's student governments, with several meetings held at Western.
money: 1,175 of Western's 11,000 students voted in the 21 October mock election

src.label: 1972 Talisman, Associated Students sections, pp. 57 and 272-73

why: Another fact-checker miss: the heading and the whole programme list are in the volume's full text, and the Homecoming dance and the mock-election turnout are on the earlier Associated Students page, which I added to the citation; date demoted to year-only.

title: Sam Ervin analyses Watergate
body: Senator Sam Ervin, chairman of the Senate Watergate committee, spoke at Western on 2 April 1974 under a contract ASG had signed in February. The Herald reported the lecture on 5 April, and in the same issue judged ASG's 1973-74 lecture series its best effort to date.
why: Cut the Talisman sentence and Representative Conyers, who is not in that volume, but the ASG tie the checker could not find is in the Herald of 15 February 1974, whose contents list an article on ASG contracting Ervin to speak on 2 April.

title: Charles Berlitz opens the ASG lecture series on the Bermuda Triangle
body: Charles Berlitz, author of The Bermuda Triangle, opened the Associated Student Government lecture series in Van Meter Auditorium on 9 September 1975. The Herald carried the advance notice that morning; the 1976 Talisman reported a standing-room-only audience and recorded that Berlitz said more than 100 planes and ships and 1,000 people had vanished in the region since 1945, and that he ran through theories from heavy magnetisation to alien beings.
why: Said plainly that the Herald item was a same-day advance notice and moved the audience and the content onto the 1976 Talisman, which I read in full text and which names ASG as the sponsor of the series.

title: Harrison Salisbury lectures
why: Nothing ties the lecture to ASG: the cited Herald item is a same-day notice naming no sponsor, and the 1976 Talisman only lists him among lecturers scheduled for the spring; the lecture itself did happen, since the Herald of 2 April 1976 (51:51, dlsc_ua_records/5141) reported his remarks on politics and US-China relations, so it can return if a sponsor is ever sourced.

title: ASG signs three lectures for the spring
body: The Herald reported on 18 January 1979 that Associated Student Government had signed three lecturers for the spring semester. The archive holds the issue as a contents listing, which does not name them.
why: Cut Dick Gregory, the 400-count and the jazz band, because the 1979 Talisman credits the Black Awareness Symposium to the university's programs coordinator and files the jazz band under Center Board, and no source names Gregory as one of ASG's three lectures; kept the single ASG fact the Herald supports.

title: ASG's International Week
body: Associated Student Government sponsored International Week, which ran nightly from Monday 10 November 1980 and closed with a presentation on Brazil and Colombia on the Thursday evening. Two or three countries were featured each night through films, lectures, folk dances and slides given by students and faculty from those countries, and programme chairman Osama Shariff opened the week with a talk on Palestine and a Red Cross film on Palestinian children. The 1981 Talisman, which spells him Sharif and calls him international students committee chairman, credits the week to student government and the International Students Committee, places the nightly programmes in the university center, and lists nine countries: Switzerland, Palestine, Iceland, Malaysia, Colombia, Brazil, India, Pakistan and France.
why: Added the 1981 Talisman, which I verified in full text, for the nine countries and the university-center venue that the Herald never gives, credited the co-organising International Students Committee, and flagged the Shariff/Sharif spelling as unresolved.

title: Mock presidential election with the College Republicans
body: ASG co-sponsored a mock presidential election with the College Republicans on Tuesday 25 October 1988, from 10:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. in the university center, with student identification cards required to vote. Public relations vice president Amos Gott said before it that the aim was to see how Western felt as a community compared with Bowling Green and with the national response to the candidates. The Herald of 27 October reported that George Bush won the mock race.
why: Cut the future-tense results-posting line and marked Gott's purpose as something said in advance, then added the 27 October issue, which I checked and which reports the result, so the event can be dated to the Tuesday it was set for.

title: Weekend in the Woods announced for 23 and 24 October
body: President Donald Smith told congress on 12 October 1993 that Weekend in the Woods would be held on 23 and 24 October. The minutes carry one line on it and record nothing about who went, where it was held or what it cost.
why: Redated to the meeting the minutes actually record, retitled as the announcement it is, and cut the claim that ASG had run the retreat since the early 1980s, which was an inference from the 1987 Talisman's "fourth annual".

title: SGA hands out flyers for a Jesse Jackson Jr. speech
body: Administrative vice president Scott Sivley passed out flyers at the congress meeting of 29 March 1994 for a speech by Jesse Jackson Jr. set for 18 April. The minutes tie SGA to the publicity and to nothing else, naming no venue, sponsor or fee, and they do not show the speech took place.
why: Redated to the meeting and refiled as a note on SGA publicity rather than an SGA-staged speaker event, since the one line in the minutes is the whole of the record.

title: Designated driver cards announced for distribution
body: The Herald of 17 February 1998 reported that the Student Government Association's designated driver cards would be distributed the following day. The archive holds the issue as a contents listing, which gives nothing about the scheme beyond the headline.
why: Corrected the issue to 73:36, cut the $900 and the free soft drinks, which are nowhere in the record, and reframed it as the announcement it is; I checked the next issue, 73:37 of 19 February, and it carries no follow-up.

title: SGA announces its spring and senior banquets
body: SGA's news page announced on 20 April 2004 that the spring banquet would take the place of the regular Congress meeting and be held in the Kentucky Building, then scheduled from 5 to 8 p.m., and that the senior banquet would follow the next Wednesday from 7.30 to 9 p.m. in the same building, with business attire asked for.

src.label: WKU SGA news page, 20 Apr 2004 (Wayback capture)

why: Redated to the announcement and dropped the held-event framing and the 27 April date: the page says the banquet was only "currently scheduled", and SGA's own calendar gives a different start time.

title: SGA funds Hidden Hacks of the Hill
body: SGA passed Bill 20-17-F at its meeting on 31 October 2017, approving $200 for fliers and refreshments for Hidden Hacks on the Hill, an event set for 14 November in DSU Nite Class to help minority and underrepresented students find campus resources. The Herald reported that WKU hosted it that Tuesday morning in Downing Student Union, with the Writing Center, the Counseling and Testing Center and the WKU Food Pantry represented, and that SGA senator Divya Gangavelli spoke on the White, Red and Purple bus lines and on riding the Grise Hall lift to the top of the Hill.

src.label: College Heights Herald, 1 Nov 2017 - Ziege, "SGA funds Day of Action to engage students with legislation"

src2.label: College Heights Herald, 16 Nov 2017 - Singleton, "Students learn the hidden hacks of the Hill"

why: Moved the SGA-funding claim onto the 1 November report of Bill 20-17-F, which I read and which gives the $200 and the date, kept the 16 November article only for what happened, and corrected the bus detail, since the hack for getting up the Hill was the Grise Hall lift and not the buses.
